name: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
problem: Autoregressive decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound: each new token requires a full pass over model weights, so decode FLOPs are wasted and accelerator compute sits idle.
mechanism: Two-model draft-verify. A small draft model autoregressively proposes K tokens; the large target model scores all K+1 positions in ONE forward pass using custom attention masks (each position attends to its own prefix of draft tokens). A modified rejection-sampling acceptance rule (accept with min(1, p_target(x)/q_draft(x))) plus resampling from the target's residual distribution makes the output distribution provably identical to plain autoregressive decoding. Requires no target-model modification.
speedup_reported: 2x-3x wall-clock speedup at temperature 0 and up to ~2.5x with temperature sampling, on T5-XXL / T5-XXL-Target (T5-11B) and LLaMA-65B, at batch size 1-64. Acceptance-rate-per-step (tau) is the number that makes the speedup meaningful; the paper reports mean acceptance length as a function of draft K and model pair. Baseline is unmodified autoregressive decoding of the same target model.
notes:
THE canonical speculative-decoding record: ICLR 2023, the origin of the draft-model-plus-modified-rejection-sampling formulation everything else (SpecInfer, Sequoia, EAGLE, Medusa) reuses. VENUE NOTE: venue/year are taken from the arXiv comment field ('ICLR 2023') cross-checked against Semantic Scholar; arXiv v1 is Nov 2022, ICLR 2023 is the venue year. Adoption is 'in-production' because the ALGORITHM (not the code) is shipped: TensorRT-LLM, vLLM (n-gram + model spec decode), llama.cpp (draft-model spec decode), and SGLang all implement draft-verify with modified rejection sampling. Hard caveat for anyone benchmarking this: at large batch size the verify pass becomes compute-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and the speedup collapses - this is exactly what MagicDec (pap-eff-magicdec) and FlashInfer-style batch-size-aware work attack. A speedup quoted without batch size and without the acceptance rate is meaningless for this technique. DANGLING REF STILL OPEN (2026-10-04 paper-read pass; supersedes the earlier 'LEFT UNRESOLVED' note, which reached the same conclusion but only from this record's own text - this time the PAPER itself was read). Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.17192 . Its one hardware sentence is generic: "the value of c depends on the hardware configuration and software implementation details". Left dangling.
